description:
FILED s473h (Opus, 2026-09-08) as the owner of ir-conform case 243-string,
taken over from #1249(3), which asked for a probe matrix and a decision.  The
matrix was measured; the decision is RULED DIVERGENCE, and this task is where
the row's ownership lives.

THE MEASUREMENT (scratch/s473h/probe/m3.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs PCL at a9f2a264;
`flag` = utf8::is_utf8, `len` = length):

    shape                        perl        PCL
    "abc"                        flag=0      flag=1
    "\x{e2}\x{80}\x{99}"         flag=0      flag=1
    "\x{2019}"                   flag=1      flag=1
    utf8::upgrade of the above   flag=1      flag=1
    utf8::decode of octets       flag=1      flag=1
    utf8::encode of a wide str   flag=0      flag=1
    42                           flag=0      flag=1
    "a" . "\x{2019}"             flag=1      flag=1
    undef                        flag=0      flag=1
    chr(233) / chr(9731)         flag=0 / 1  flag=1
    join / sprintf / pack A3     flag=0      flag=1
    substr of a wide string      flag=1      flag=1

  LENGTH agrees in all 15 rows.  This is introspection only.

WHY NO CHEAPER TRUTH EXISTS (the two candidate rules, both measured):

(a) "1 iff the string holds a character > 0xFF" gets 14 of the 15 rows right
    -- but the ONE it misses is `utf8::upgrade`, and that is precisely the row
    ir-conform 243-string pins:

        my $s = "\x{e2}\x{80}\x{99}";  # perl flag=0   <- the only line that
        utf8::upgrade($s);             # perl flag=1      differs today

    Under (a) the upgraded string still answers 0, so the case does not pass
    and the corpus gains nothing, while every `is_utf8` after an
    Encode/utf8::decode of pure-ASCII octets would start answering 0 where
    perl says 1 -- a NEW divergence in the direction real code consults.

(b) a per-scalar flag set by utf8::upgrade would need a BOX slot, and it would
    not survive `my $c = $s` (a copy makes a fresh box), where perl's SV flag
    does.  s335 ruled out a new box slot for the referent-kind question
    (#154); this is the same shape and the same answer.

THE RULING.  perl's flag means "this SV is in the UPGRADED (character) form".
In PCL EVERY string is in that form -- CL strings are character strings and
there is no downgraded representation to report.  So **1 is the honest answer
for PCL's model**, and answering 0 for a byte-only string would claim a
downgraded form that does not exist.  `docs/not-supported.md` ("The per-scalar
UTF-8 flag") carries the ruling and this task number.

WHAT WOULD REOPEN IT: a PCL string representation that has a byte form (an
octet-string type distinct from a character string).  That is a data-model
change, not an is_utf8 fix.

CORPUS: ir-conform/known-fail.tsv row `243-string` re-pointed from 1249 to
this task.  The case's other five lines (upgrade / decode / bad decode / wide /
narrow) all match perl already -- only the `before:` line differs.
subject: RULED DIVERGENCE (s473h): utf8::is_utf8 always answers 1 because PCL has no DOWNGRADED form -- the ir-conform 243-string row's owner, taken over from #1249(3)
